records.justification: The agent's text accurately summarizes the purpose of the Butterfield Awards as described in the provided page text.

claims.text: Butterfield Awards support exchanges and collaborations between health and medical professionals in Japan and the UK.
The awards can support the study of scientific, clinical, social and economic issues in healthcare.

records.justification: The agent's text captures all eligibility criteria mentioned in the reference text but omits all purpose-related claims.

claims.text: Applicants must belong to, or provide evidence of support from, an organisation or institution willing to receive grant funds.
Individuals seeking support for personal projects are not accepted.
The UK office may consider individuals with organisational backing.
Undergraduate or master's students are not supported.
Grant payments cannot be made to personal bank accounts.
UK-originating projects apply to the UK office.

Grant money can be used to support festivals, workshops, performances and other events that present aspects of Japan to the UK or the UK to Japan in cultural, scientific, social, sporting and other spheres.

Grant money can be used to support exchanges between the UK and Japan that enable participation and interaction, for instance of schools and sporting groups, artists, artisans, performers, scientists and researchers.
Grant money can be used to support collaborative projects involving UK and Japanese participants that result in new and innovative outputs for public, academic or professional presentation.
Grant money can be used to support the teaching and development of Japanese language and cultural studies in schools, and higher education.
Grant money can be used to support academic research, visits and exchange, where these push forward the boundaries of knowledge and understanding or involve collaboration and co-production.

records.justification: The agent's text supports most eligibility criteria but omits requirements regarding project partners, referees, and the application office.

claims.text: Applicants should normally show an existing research record.
Consideration will be given to practitioners, managers, carers or others in health-related fields intending to establish working links or produce a publishable comparative study.
Projects must involve partners in both the UK and Japan.
Projects must be supported by two referees from different institutions to the project partners.
Applications should be made to the UK office.
Preference is given to those new to UK-Japan collaboration.
Preference is given to early-career applicants.

records.justification: The agent's text accurately reflects the eligibility criteria stated in the page text regarding organizational affiliation and the conditions under which individuals can apply.

claims.text: Applicants should normally have an existing research record.
